gaps.sentence: There's ___ at the door — go and see who it is.
gaps.explanation: 'Somebody' is used in affirmative sentences for an unknown person; 'anybody' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.hint: an unspecified day in the future
gaps.explanation: 'Another day' means some other, unspecified day; 'the other day' refers to the recent past.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the equipment has been serviced this year, so breakdowns are rare.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of + noun' = the majority of it; 'the most' is a superlative.

gaps.sentence: Very ___ applicants had the required experience.
gaps.hint: 'very' + negative quantifier with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Very few' means almost none and is used with countables; 'very a few' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The box was empty — there was ___ inside.
gaps.explanation: 'Empty' explains 'there was nothing inside'; the other options contradict emptiness.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: Some metals are magnetic; ___ are not.
gaps.explanation: 'Some ... others ...' contrasts unspecified groups; 'the others' would need a closed, known set.
